High grade ductal carcinoma in situ with necrosis in several expanded ducts within fibrotic breast stroma. Malignant in situ carcinoma cells show marked nuclear pleomorphism with mitoses. A large duct is similarly affected by high grade DCIS, displaying luminal haemorrhage and surrounded by inflamed fibrous stroma containing foamy histiocytes and cholesterol clefts.

diagnosis: Low and intermediate nuclear grade DCIS, dimorphic pattern.
legend: Many ducts are expanded by a dimorphic population of monomorphic cells which are centrally darker with smaller hyperchromatic nuclei, and peripherally paler with larger vesicular nuclei. Immunohistochemistry shows diffuse nuclear reactivity for ER, while CK5/6 and CK14 decorate the intact rim of myoepithelial cells without any staining of the epithelial population, corroborating the diagnosis of DCIS of low to intermediate nuclear grade, without necrosis. Papillary DCIS with a similar neoplastic population is present. Occasional calcifications are discerned.

diagnosis: Apocrine ductal carcinoma in situ, intermediate to high nuclear grade with focal necrosis and calcifications.
legend:
Apocrine ductal carcinoma in situ with underlying sclerosing adenosis
Breast core biopsies show apocrine DCIS, intermediate to high nuclear grade with necrosis and calcifications, superimposed on underlying sclerosing adenosis with columnar cell change and atypical ductal hyperplasia.

diagnosis: Ductal carcinoma in situ, low and intermediate nuclear grade, without necrosis or calcifications, predominantly papillary and focally cribriform patterns.
legend:
Ductal carcinoma in situ, low and intermediate nuclear grade, without necrosis or calcifications, predominantly papillary and focally cribriform
Vacuum assisted breast biopsy shows ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) with predominant papillary to focal cribriform architecture and low to intermediate nuclear grade, without necrosis or calcifications. Occasional small entrapped squamoid nests limited to the inflamed fibrous walls of papillary DCIS are present. No invasive carcinoma is seen.

diagnosis: Ductal carcinoma in situ, low nuclear grade and intermediate to high nuclear grade with necrosis, without calcifications
legend:
Ductal carcinoma in situ, low nuclear grade and intermediate to high nuclear grade with necrosis, without calcifications

Two areas of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) of different nuclear grades merge with each other, spanning an overall extent of 20 mm. One area comprises solid and cribriform architectural growth patterns with low nuclear grade devoid of necrosis superimposed on underlying sclerosing adenosis. The second area consists of cribriform, clinging and micropapillary patterns, with intermediate to focally high nuclear grade and apocrine morphology as well as focal necrosis in a background of a radial sclerosing lesion. 

Immunohistochemistry for ER shows diffuse positivity in low nuclear grade DCIS while PR is expressed in about 50% of DCIS cells
This contrasts against the negative ER and PR staining in the intermediate to high nuclear grade DCIS component.
CK5 shows an intact myoepithelial layer around DCIS, with loss of staining in the neoplastic epithelial population.

legend:
Ductal carcinoma in situ, intermediate and high nuclear grade, without necrosis or calcifications, hypersecretory type
Vacuum assisted breast biopsies show enlarged lobules with acini featuring secretory changes lined by clinging type abnormal epithelial cells displaying moderate to markedly pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei and vacuolated cytoplasm with luminal pink eosinophilic colloid like secretions. No necrosis or calcifications are identified.
